summary.business_type: B2B AI implementation agency (service business, STR/real-estate/med-spa vertical focus)
top_findings: Six of eight pages declare the homepage as their canonical, instructing Google not to index them
Five pages share a byte-identical title tag and meta description
/work carries 2,789 words of portfolio content and is canonicalised away to the homepage
No page contains a self-contained answer block; longest paragraph on the homepage is 37 words
Zero percentages and zero dollar figures appear in extractable text across the site
quick_wins: Set a self-referencing canonical on /about, /services, /work, /book and /webinar
Write unique title tags and meta descriptions for those five pages
Remove the duplicated brand suffix in the /webinar title
Add width and height to the six homepage images missing them
Publish real pricing figures as quotable text

categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: HTTPS enforced, clean 200 responses across all eight sitemap URLs
robots.txt present, valid, and explicitly permissive to AI search crawlers
sitemap.xml present and valid at /sitemap.xml with 8 URLs
meta robots is index, follow with no X-Robots-Tag override

findings.title: Six of eight pages canonicalise to the homepage
findings.description: /about, /services, /work, /book and /webinar all emit <link rel="canonical" href="https://solnestai.com">. Verified directly against raw HTML, not through a parser. A canonical pointing at a different URL tells Google the page is a duplicate and should not be indexed in its own right. These are not duplicates: /work alone holds 2,789 words of unique portfolio content.
findings.recommendation: Emit a self-referencing canonical on every page. /about should declare https://solnestai.com/about, and so on. This is almost certainly one shared layout component hardcoding the site root.

findings.title: Core Web Vitals could not be measured
findings.description: PageSpeed Insights returned a rate-limit error because no API key is configured. No field or lab data was collected, so no CWV claim is made in this report.
findings.recommendation: Run /solnest-seo:seo google setup to add a free Google API key, then re-run for real CrUX field data.

categories.name: On-Page SEO
what_works: Every page has exactly one H1
Heading hierarchy is clean, with 24 H3s under 8 H2s on the homepage
Homepage carries 17 internal links and a coherent structure

findings.title: Five pages share an identical title tag and meta description
findings.description: /, /about, /services, /work and /book all use the title "Solnest AI - Watch What Happens When AI Meets Your Business" and the same meta description verbatim. Duplicate titles across a small site are a strong duplicate-content signal and waste the highest-value on-page ranking element on four pages.
findings.recommendation: Write a unique, intent-matched title and description per page. /services should target the service query, /work the proof query, /about the entity query.

findings.title: Duplicated brand suffix in the /webinar title
findings.description: The title reads "Live Demo - From Zero to Automated | Solnest AI | Solnest AI", repeating the brand twice. This is the signature of a template appending a suffix to a title that already contains one.
findings.recommendation: Strip the brand from the page-level title or make the template suffix conditional.

categories.name: Content Quality
what_works: /work is substantial at 2,789 words
The blog post is a genuine 947-word comparison piece with 4 schema blocks
Copy is specific about verticals: short-term rentals, real estate, med spas

findings.title: Four pages are thin
findings.description: /book is 52 words, /blog is 59, /about is 292 and /webinar is 317. /about at 292 words is well short of what an entity-establishing page needs, and it is one of the pages AI systems read to decide who a company is.
findings.recommendation: Prioritise /about and /services. Both are commercially important and both are currently too thin to rank or be cited.

categories.name: Schema and Structured Data
what_works: Organization and ProfessionalService JSON-LD present on every page
Correct use of @id anchors such as #organization and #service
Blog post carries 4 schema blocks including article-level markup
Organization name is byte-identical to every other brand surface

findings.title: Schema is duplicated rather than page-specific
findings.description: The same Organization and ProfessionalService pair appears on all pages. That is valid and harmless, but page-type schema is missing where it would earn rich results.
findings.recommendation: Add Service schema on /services and FAQPage where genuine Q&A exists. Note this is a rich-results play, not an AI-citation lever.

categories.name: Images
what_works: Zero missing alt attributes across all 8 pages, which is unusual and good

findings.title: Six homepage images lack width and height
findings.description: 6 of 9 homepage images declare no intrinsic dimensions, which allows layout shift while they load and harms Cumulative Layout Shift.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit width and height, or use the Next.js Image component which sets them automatically.

findings.title: Only one image is lazy-loaded
findings.recommendation: Lazy-load everything below the fold, keeping the LCP image eager.

categories.name: AI Search Readiness
what_works: All four search crawlers allowed in robots.txt and returning 200 at the CDN edge: OAI-SearchBot (ChatGPT), Claude-SearchBot (Claude), PerplexityBot (Perplexity), Googlebot (Google AI Overviews)

robots.txt correctly separates search crawlers from training crawlers, which most sites get wrong. OAI-SearchBot and Claude-SearchBot control citation; GPTBot and ClaudeBot are training only; Google-Extended has no effect on AI Overviews
Snippet-eligible: index, follow with no X-Robots-Tag override
Brand entity is byte-identical across all 5 machine-readable surfaces: title, og:site_name, jsonld:Organization, jsonld:ProfessionalService, llms.txt
AI visibility band: Readable

findings.title: Five pages are canonicalised to the homepage, blocking AI retrieval
findings.description: Google AI Overviews and AI Mode retrieve from the ordinary Search index. /about, /services, /work, /book and /webinar all declare https://solnestai.com as canonical, so they are not eligible to be retrieved or cited. Verified against raw HTML.
findings.recommendation: Emit self-referencing canonicals. This is the single highest-leverage fix for both search and AI visibility.

findings.title: Nothing on the site is quotable
findings.description: Main-content extraction yields 479 words from 1,921. The longest paragraph is 37 words against a 134 to 167 word target, with zero paragraphs over 40 words. Extractable text contains 0 percentages and 0 dollar figures. A model can read the page and has nothing to lift and attribute.
findings.recommendation: Add two or three genuine 130 to 160 word answer blocks with real numbers. Published pricing is the most quotable asset available and is absent from extractable text.

findings.title: Only two of eight homepage H2s are question-form
findings.description: Question-shaped headings match how people phrase prompts and how retrieval segments a page.
findings.recommendation: Convert several H2s to the questions buyers actually ask.

findings.title: Citability measurements
findings.description: Extraction yields 479 of 1921 words (25%). Longest paragraph 37 words against a 134-167 target. Paragraphs over 40 words: 0. Percentages: 0. Dollar figures: 0. Question-form H2s: 2/8.
findings.recommendation: Track these on re-audit. They are the concrete measures behind the citability score.
